reports.summary: Build I does what the task asks. Parameter.spec, Option.spec and Argument.spec match every example in the task. get_help_spec is now on Parameter, and Argument overrides it to return its metavar. Error messages and deprecation messages quote the spec. human_readable_name warns and returns spec, and a Parameter subclass that defines it warns at class definition, with the correct stacklevel. A Base(Option) that overrides it warns once, and its Child subclasses do not warn again. The one real gap is a mixin that is not a Parameter subclass: it can override human_readable_name without any warning, because only `cls.__dict__` is checked. The tests are meaningful and parametrized (34 new cases). The docs and changelog are thorough, but the changelog bullets have no PR reference. Every required check passes. A maintainer would likely merge this after small edits.

judges.verdict: All nine builds pass pytest, mypy and both ruff checks, and all produce the required spec, deprecation-message and human_readable_name behaviour, so what separates them is API care rather than core correctness. A ranks first: it is the only build that catches an override of human_readable_name coming from a mixin, and it keeps the Option.get_help_spec help-column hook from 8.5.1. E, C, I and H match the design of Click's main branch closely. B, D and G took the instruction to move get_help_spec literally, so Option.get_help_spec now returns only the spec, and overriding it no longer changes --help: in B and D for options and arguments, in G for options. That silent break of a recently public API is why those three rank last. The inspector's single 'major' defect, the mixin gap in I, does exist, but it is minor: eight builds share it and Click's main branch has it too.
